summary: Pre-stage disabled Fractal services and explicitly cut over one default host with same-filesystem config/state renames

replay.detail: No stored history or replay change; the existing state directory is renamed, not copied or rewritten.

schema.detail: No database or claim schema change.

rules.detail: No checkpoint or coordination rule change. Cutover refuses pending checkpoints and active or unobserved replication.

compatibility.detail: Normal installers still write legacy names. Explicit service install --stage-fractal and Home Manager fractalMigration.phase=stage prepare disabled target definitions without restarting legacy services. fractal migrate host renames default XDG st3 config/state directories to fractal, moves complete service drop-in directories, writes exact destination receipts, and bridges the old directory paths with symlinks. Named instances and workspace roots are not moved. Both service families running, missing staging, cross-filesystem moves, or nonempty destinations are hard errors.

downtime.detail: No cutover happens automatically. An explicit per-host cutover briefly stops the legacy daemon before starting the pre-staged target, checks local API readiness instead of Type=simple, and reports the measured gap plus unchanged effective Linux memory.swap.max and MemoryLow.

manual.detail: Coordinate one host at a time, never during checkpoint or sync. Stage definitions, run fractal migrate host --dry-run, then fractal migrate host --json and retain the receipt. Move unrelated dotfiles Fractal TUI data to fractalite before using populated Fractal destinations. After Home Manager cutover select phase=completed before activating again. See docs/upgrading-st.md.

recovery.detail: Legacy boot/login activation is disabled before any move; atomic config/state bridge exchanges never expose an absent old root. Receipts are atomically published. Pre-readiness rollback restores original enablement and config objects and persists reverse progress so recovery can itself be retried. Home Manager keeps a foreign config symlink fence against immutable old generations, including backup modes; preflight scans retained profile generations and lists generation numbers to prune when forced targets raw-prefix-match legacy config/state paths, refusing uninspectable definitions without execution. Once readiness commits, rollback is refused and rerunning finishes legacy retirement. macOS installer rollback restores staged plist absence, exact symlink objects, and prior effective enablement without loading jobs.
